model.description: Provider model id of the THINKING model; the template carries ctx.model (strict, resolved at instantiation). Convention (K-H2): pass a RESOLVED literal. R-CG-1: the core is allowed to take longer than the channel voice, so the shipped timeouts are the long ones - a channel-voice model here wastes the split.

credential_grant_id.description: GH #560: the grant this brain presents to get its bearer credential SEALED from an access hive, instead of carrying it in `api_key`. It ships EMPTY, which is no grant at all -- the cell then behaves exactly as it did before and spends `api_key`. Set it (normally through `override_params` of the manifest that grows the generation) and the member's own broker answers: the credential arrives over the credential v-lane, is opened in this task's RAM and is written nowhere. WHICH credential is named by the grant and never here, so a cell cannot ask for a secret it was not granted (R-AC-2). Since GH #138 it is a plain param and not an environment token: a grant id is a REFERENCE, and two generations in one colony present different ones.

credential_wait_ms.description: GH #457: how long one sealed credential round may take before every parked turn gets its `credential_pending` receipt. The substrate default is 10 s, which was measured against a broker standing beside the consumer; a member's broker is three python cells and two store round trips away from a brain four levels down, so this template ships the longer one. It bounds nothing but the WAIT -- no provider is called and nothing is billed while it runs.

description.purpose: The agent core's one inference (R-CG-1): reasoning, LLM-backed tool work and everything a channel voice hands over. Its system state - identity, core instructions, tool schemas - accumulates in its own cell.db, one writer per system path. The memory bundle of the central hive is NOT part of that state: since collector 2.1.0 it arrives per round as a synthetic memory_recall tool result in messages[] and expires with that round (GH #278).
description.use_when: Inside the cogny composite, behind the collector's seam. Slower and stronger than a talky brain on purpose; the whole point of the advisor split is that nobody waits for this call.
description.not_in_scope: No tool execution, no context assembly, no channel persona. Cogny never speaks to a user directly - it answers the channel voice, which verbalises the result in its own tone. Provider and auth are instance business: the shipped default is the OpenRouter chat lane, a subscription or another provider is override_params.
description.emits_meaning: finish_reason 'stop'/'tool_calls' -> ./dispatcher (the dispatcher tells a final answer from a tool bundle); 'length' -> the collector's in_answer lane (a truncated answer is an answer); 'error'/'content_filter' -> the parent's drain, wired from ./brain, because an error echo carries the PROMPT back and must never be filed as the core's own words.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[] the assembled errand of one consultation - the talky IS this brain's user. A body with system but WITHOUT messages is a system update: it upserts the slot and triggers no inference.
examples: a consult errand -> tool_calls -> the core's own tool round -> the same seam again with iter+1 -> stop, and the advice leaves on the answer lane
a consultation the core cannot finish alone -> stop with a question, which travels the SAME return lane and reaches the user through the channel voice
